arguments.question: Why does secondary (settling) performance remain unmet in this execution even though terminal reach succeeded? Recorded summary: reach_passed = true with terminal_error_m = 0.0076 against reach_tolerance_m = 0.01, but sampled_settling_passed = false, with a late-window late_max_speed_m_s = 1.581 (vs speed_limit_m_s = 0.02) and late_max_error_m = 0.0581 (vs position_limit_m = 0.01) over a 0.05 s window, in a run where every update missed its deadline (deadline_misses = 35, stopping_counts User_Requested_Stop = 34, Solve_Succeeded = 1) and mean_update_s = 17.075 against control_period_s = 0.01, with horizon = 10, max_iterations = 120, max_cpu_s = 30.0, and a bundled_guess numerical_source. The question is open: which of the retained signals — per-update solve/status behaviour, plan/iteration selection, effective horizon, applied versus requested tension, projected-state evolution, sampled backend motion at matched endpoints — are consistent with a sustained late-window tip speed and position error after reach, and which remain indeterminate with available evidence? No root cause is presumed; a single bounded projected-model probe over a 10 ms horizon cannot by itself explain an entire settling failure and must not be presented as doing so.
